pack.name: live-lab
pack.description: Live lab scenarios: harmless child processes and a loopback listener observed by the real collector. Skipped by synthetic runs; executed only with --live in a verified lab.

scenarios.title: Parent-child chain observed on a live host
scenarios.description: The lab starts a chain of three sleeping Python processes. The collector must record the root as a child of the runner and a descendant under the root.
scenarios.objective: The real collector reports the expected process relationships, and no rule fires on harmless sleeping processes.

telemetry.description: the chain root is a child of the validation runner
a child exists under the chain root

cleanup.description: Every child process the run started is terminated and its exit verified; only files below the lab directory were created (evidence is kept there).

limitations: Runs on a real host, so the collected telemetry also contains whatever else that host is doing; only detections that involve records the lab created are judged, and the number of others is reported.
A pass shows the collector and engine handled these harmless activities on this host and OS version; it does not generalise to other hosts.
Unprivileged collection leaves coverage partial by design (see the coverage fields).

scenarios.title: Loopback listener observed with its owner
scenarios.description: The lab starts a child that listens on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port. The collector must record the listener, its address and its owning process.
scenarios.objective: Listener ownership is resolved by the real collector on this host, and nothing fires on a loopback listener.

telemetry.description: its owner is the lab child

limitations: Runs on a real host, so the collected telemetry also contains whatever else that host is doing; only detections that involve records the lab created are judged, and the number of others is reported.

scenarios.title: Categories that were not collected are reported as not collected
scenarios.description: Collection is restricted to processes. Rules that need authentication events or listeners must say they were not collected.
scenarios.objective: The real collector's coverage statements drive honest 'inconclusive' results instead of a clean report.

cleanup.description: Every child process the run started is terminated and its exit verified; only files below the lab directory were created (evidence is kept there).

limitations: Runs on a real host, so the collected telemetry also contains whatever else that host is doing; only detections that involve records the lab created are judged, and the number of others is reported.

Process coverage is complete only when every executable link is readable (root or an elevated shell); otherwise it is partial and this scenario reports that difference as a failure of its first coverage check.
